searchText: Hi guys, one question related to the EVM. I'm analyzing EVM bytecode taken from ethereum sepolia testnet and I find a lot of opcodes that do not correspond with any known opcode. They are not valid opcodes, I think it's possible to upload a contract that has invalid opcodes and the EVM should revert when it finds a not known opcode. Then I found out that there is a specific opcode that is 0xFE which is the INVALID opcode. What is the difference between INVALID 0xFE opcode and all others not known opcodes? I mean, the EVM reverts in all cases, but, a part from that, are there any other differences? And also what is the rational behind having the INVALID 0xFE opcode? Having 0xfe as the invalid opcode is just a convention, so contract developers can be sure that this opcode WILL NEVER be assigned to anything. But yes unassigned opcodes have the same behavior as the INVALID opcode. Are you sure you are not mistaken immediates for opcodes though? The push opcodes have immediates which can be arbitrary data yes I know this thank you very much, I'm filtering out push data in order to have only opcodes. Ok so it's just a convention thanks a lot.

Hi guys, one question related to the EVM. I'm analyzing EVM bytecode taken from ethereum sepolia testnet and I find a lot of opcodes that do not correspond with any known opcode.

They are not valid opcodes, I think it's possible to upload a contract that has invalid opcodes and the EVM should revert when it finds a not known opcode. Then I found out that there is a specific opcode that is 0xFE which is the INVALID opcode.

What is the difference between INVALID 0xFE opcode and all others not known opcodes? I mean, the EVM reverts in all cases, but, a part from that, are there any other differences? And also what is the rational behind having the INVALID 0xFE opcode?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Having 0xfe as the invalid opcode is just a convention, so contract developers can be sure that this opcode WILL NEVER be assigned to anything. But yes unassigned opcodes have the same behavior as the INVALID opcode.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Are you sure you are not mistaken immediates for opcodes though? The push opcodes have immediates which can be arbitrary data

excerpts.author: alemaz98
excerpts.content: yes I know this thank you very much, I'm filtering out push data in order to have only opcodes. Ok so it's just a convention thanks a lot.
